title: NY State Assembly · District 25
area: North-central Queens, including Fresh Meadows, Pomonok, Electchester, Kew Gardens Hills and parts of Flushing and Briarwood.

context.text: Incumbent Nily Rozic is running unopposed in the November 3, 2026 general election. Her only prospective challenger, Kenneth Paek, was ruled off the ballot for both the Republican primary and an independent "4 Our Immigrants Party" line.

summary.text: Nily Rozic is the Democratic incumbent for NY State Assembly District 25 in eastern Queens, first elected in 2012. Born in Jerusalem and raised in Queens, she was chief of staff to Assemblymember Brian Kavanagh before her election. She chairs the Assembly Consumer Affairs and Protection Committee and also serves on the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions, Labor, Rules and Ways and Means committees. She is running unopposed for re-election in 2026.

background.text: Was born in Jerusalem and raised in Queens, according to her official Assembly biography.
Graduated from New York University and from Syracuse University's Maxwell School of Citizenship and Public Affairs; NYU honored her with a Distinguished Young Alumni Award in 2022.
Worked as Chief of Staff to Assemblymember Brian Kavanagh before her own election to the Assembly.
Served as a member of Community Board 8 and of the Townsend Harris High School Alumni Association before her election, according to her official biography.

Elected to the Assembly in 2012; her official biography says she became the youngest woman in the state legislature and the first woman to represent the 25th District, which includes Flushing, Fresh Meadows, Bayside, Douglaston and other eastern Queens communities.

Currently chairs the Committee on Consumer Affairs and Protection and sits on the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions, Labor, Rules, and Ways and Means committees. She previously chaired the Subcommittee on Emerging Workforce, the Task Force on Women's Issues (2017) and the Office on State-Federal Relations (2020).
According to her official biography, she has sponsored legislation on workplace flexibility, fair work shifts and pay equity, and authored a law easing work schedules for state employees.

Was named to City & State's 2013 list of the Next Generation of Political Leaders and The Jewish Week's 36 Under 36, and took part in the Lindsay Fellowship Program's inaugural class (2017) at CUNY's Institute for Local and State Governance; she lives in Fresh Meadows, according to her official biography.

positions.summary: Sponsored A01832, authorizing a state personal income tax credit for residential solar energy systems.

record.text: Chairs the Assembly Consumer Affairs and Protection Committee (2021-2026); also serves on the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions, Labor, Rules, and Ways and Means committees.

Sponsored A00255, directing the state Attorney General to write rules against price gouging on fuel, energy and transportation goods and requiring periodic public disclosure of fuel prices along the supply chain; referred to the Consumer Affairs and Protection Committee, not enacted as of January 2026.
Sponsored A06571, establishing a comprehensive sexual and reproductive health program; reported to the Ways and Means Committee as of January 2026, not enacted.

Sponsored A08962 (as amended, A08962-B), the "FAIR news act," requiring transparency disclosures for news media content composed, authored, or otherwise created through generative AI; passed the Assembly on June 5, 2026 (substituted by the Senate's companion bill, S08451-B) and returned to the Senate, not enacted as of this writing.
Sponsored A01832, authorizing a personal income tax credit for residential solar energy systems; referred to the Ways and Means Committee, not enacted as of January 2026.

researchNotes: Rozic's only prospective 2026 opponent, Kenneth Paek, was disqualified from both the Republican primary and an independent ballot line, leaving her unopposed on the November 3 general-election ballot. No opposing candidate entry is included because none will appear on the ballot. Two floor-vote claims (S10113, S3460) were removed on verification: the cited Assembly bill pages show only referral/passage actions, not the individual member's vote or the floor tally, and that data could not be confirmed from any reachable source.
